# F4: the full reference

> F4 is a free, open-source sticker app for macOS, like WhatsApp stickers but for the whole Mac: a Spotlight-like floating panel that searches a local library of stickers (PNG, WebP, GIF, JPEG, animated ones included) and copies one to the clipboard in a keystroke, ready to paste anywhere. This file is everything an AI assistant or agent needs to install F4, explain it, or help someone use it. The short version is https://f4.kkratter.com/llms.txt. To change F4's code, read https://github.com/kkratterf/f4/blob/main/AGENTS.md instead.

## At a glance

- Platform: macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple Silicon and Intel (universal binary). No iOS, Windows or Linux version.
- License: MIT. Price: free. Source: https://github.com/kkratterf/f4
- Website: https://f4.kkratter.com/ (English) and https://f4.kkratter.com/it/ (Italian); FAQ: https://f4.kkratter.com/faq/
- Bundle identifier: `com.kkratterf.f4`. The app is `F4.app`; it has no Dock icon and lives in the menu bar.
- Languages: English, and Italian when macOS runs in Italian.
- Privacy: no analytics, no account, no server. Files are read locally. F4 goes online only for the update check against https://f4.kkratter.com/appcast.xml (turned off with `defaults write com.kkratterf.f4 SUEnableAutomaticChecks -bool false`), to download a link the user pastes or drops into the panel, and to download a pack the user switches on in the menu bar's Packs.
- Permissions: none needed.
- The name comes from "F4, basito", the stunned face of Stanis in the Italian TV series Boris.

## Install

All methods install the same app. Pick one.

1. DMG: download https://github.com/kkratterf/f4/releases/latest/download/F4.dmg (always the newest stable version), open it, drag F4 onto Applications, eject the disk image.
2. One line in Terminal:

   ```sh
   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kkratterf/f4/main/install.sh | sh
   ```

   It downloads the latest release, checks its SHA-256 against `SHA256SUMS.txt`, quits a running F4, installs `F4.app` in `/Applications` (or `~/Applications` when `/Applications` is not writable), clears the quarantine flag and offers to open it. Options go after the pipe, as environment variables:
   - `F4_VERSION=v0.2.0` installs a specific release.
   - `F4_INSTALL_DIR=~/Apps` installs somewhere else.
   - `F4_NO_OPEN=1` skips the offer to open F4.

   Example: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kkratterf/f4/main/install.sh | F4_NO_OPEN=1 sh`
3. Homebrew (the repository is its own tap):

   ```sh
   brew tap kkratterf/f4 https://github.com/kkratterf/f4
   brew install --cask f4
   ```

   The cask is marked `auto_updates`, so `brew upgrade` leaves F4 to update itself.

Every release on https://github.com/kkratterf/f4/releases ships `F4-x.y.z.zip`, `F4-x.y.z.dmg`, `F4.dmg` (the same DMG under a fixed name) and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. Verify with `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing`.

### First launch and Gatekeeper

F4 is not notarized by Apple yet, so the first launch of a copy from the DMG or the zip shows "Apple could not verify F4 is free of malware" (or "cannot verify the developer"). To open it:

1. Open F4 once and close the warning.
2. System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll down, click "Open Anyway" next to the message about F4, enter the Mac password.

Or, in Terminal: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/F4.app`. The install script does this already. It is needed once per downloaded version, not after automatic updates.

### Where is it after installing?

F4 has no Dock icon and no window at launch. Press F4 (fn-F4 on a Mac keyboard, see Options below), or click the F4 key icon in the menu bar, top right. F4 adds itself to the login items on the first launch (macOS shows a notification; System Settings > General > Login Items removes it).

## Use

1. Put stickers in the library: paste (Command-V) or drop them in the panel, or switch on a pack in the menu bar's Packs. The library is `~/Library/Application Support/F4/Memes` by default (F4's own folder, which gets a copy of the starter pack on the first launch; users upgrading with files in `~/Pictures/Memes` keep that folder). Supported files: GIF, PNG, JPEG, WebP (`.gif`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.webp`). Other files, hidden files and packages are ignored. Subfolders up to four levels deep are scanned and become categories.
2. Press F4 (fn-F4 on a Mac keyboard) in any app. The panel appears centred on the screen with the mouse, above every window, including full-screen apps.
3. Type to search, then press Enter. The sticker is on the clipboard and a "Copied to Clipboard" toast shows at the bottom of the screen for about a second (it takes no clicks or focus); paste it with Command-V wherever you want it.

In the panel:

| Key or action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Typing | Fuzzy search on file names, category (subfolder) names and tags: each word of the query must appear with its letters in order, not necessarily together ("tif" finds "this is fine"); case, accents, `-`, `_` and `.` are ignored |
| Arrow keys | Move the selection in the grid |
| Tab / Shift-Tab, ⌘1…⌘9 | Switch between the tabs: Stickers, Favourites, then one per top-level folder (remembered between launches). Stickers shows every file of the library; Favourites shows only the favourites, and stickers added while it is open become favourites; a folder tab shows that folder and its subfolders, and stickers added while it is open go into it. Search filters inside the current tab |
| Enter, or a click | Copy the selected sticker and close the panel |
| VoiceOver, Reduce Motion | VoiceOver reads each sticker's name, folder, tags and whether it is a favourite or animated, announces the sticker the arrow keys select, and offers Copy and Add to Favourites as actions. With Reduce Motion on, the selected GIF does not play (the copy is still animated) |
| Drag a sticker out | Drop the sticker's file into another app (a chat, a document, Finder): the same file as a copy, so a GIF stays animated. The panel stays open; dropping it back on the panel does nothing |
| Escape, or a click outside | Close the panel |
| ⌘V with an empty search field | Add what the clipboard holds (an opaque PNG or JPEG, such as a photo or a meme, becomes a 512×512 PNG sticker: the whole picture fitted into the square, the rest transparent, nothing cut or added; transparent PNGs, GIF and WebP are kept exactly as they are; ⌥⌘V keeps any picture as it is): an image (for example a WhatsApp or Telegram sticker copied with right-click → Copy), image files copied in Finder, a WhatsApp sticker pack file (`.wastickers`, a zip of WebP stickers with `title.txt`), a link to an image or a `.wastickers` file, or the link of a getstickerpack.com pack (its page, `https://getstickerpack.com/stickers/<pack>`, or the long "Add to WhatsApp" link), which downloads the pack's stickers (`sticker_1`, `sticker_2`... until one is missing) into a folder named after the pack. An image is saved at the top of the library (or in the folder of the open folder tab), named after its caption read with Vision text recognition, else after what it shows (Vision image classification, an English label such as "cat"), else "sticker", and tagged with up to three things it shows (Finder tags); all of it on the Mac; a pack is unpacked into a folder named after its title (the tray icon is left out). Nothing overwrites a file, and the first new sticker is selected. Any other text pastes in the search field |
| Drop on the panel | The same, for files, stickers dragged out of an app, images and links. Press the shortcut while dragging to open the panel under the pointer |
| Command-D | Add the selected sticker to Favourites, or remove it |
| Command-K | Open the actions for the selected sticker, Raycast style: Copy, Add to Favourites, Move to Folder…, Rename…, Edit Tags…, Show in Finder, Move to Trash. Type to filter, arrows to move, Enter to run, Escape or Command-K to close |
| Command-M | Move the selected sticker: Top Level, each folder of the library, New Folder… (a list like Command-K's) |
| Command-R | Rename the selected sticker |
| Command-T | Edit the selected sticker's tags, comma separated. They are the file's Finder tags (Finder shows them too, and they follow the file); search matches them, and the footer shows them |
| Command-Delete | Move the selected sticker to the Trash (with an empty search field) |
| Right-click a sticker | Copy, Add to Favourites / Remove from Favourites, Move To ▸ (Top Level, each folder of the library, New Folder…), Rename…, Edit Tags…, Show in Finder, Move to Trash. A move or rename never overwrites a file ("name 2"), and favourites and recents follow the file. Starter stickers listed from the app bundle only have Copy and Favourites, in this menu and in Command-K |
| The global shortcut again | Hide the panel |
| Drag the search bar or the bottom bar | Move the panel. It snaps to the screen's centre lines and to its default height, with a guide line, and reopens where it was left (on the screen with the mouse, at the same relative place). Drag it back to the default spot to reset |

Starter pack: F4 ships with twelve meme cats (`maramao/`). They live inside F4.app. On the first launch with F4's own library, F4 copies them into it once, so they are ordinary files to move, rename or delete, and deleted ones do not come back. With a folder of the user's own they are listed read-only after the user's stickers instead, and "Show Starter Pack" in the menu bar menu hides them. Up to 0.6 the starter pack also had animated emoji (`Emoji/`) and text stickers drawn in code (`F4/`); 0.7 moves those that are still where F4 put them to the Trash, once, and keeps any other file in those folders.

Order of results: with an empty search, favourites first under a "Favourites" heading (click the star in a sticker's corner, or Command-D, to add or remove one), then, under "Everything else", recently copied stickers (the last 30, most recent first), then the rest in folder order. While typing, the best matches come first (consecutive letters and word starts score higher), and equal matches keep that order. Only the selected sticker animates (moving the mouse over a sticker selects it, as in Raycast, but after a key press only once the mouse moves about 24 points, so the arrow keys keep their choice); the others show their first frame.

New, renamed or deleted files in the folder appear without a restart: F4 watches the folder with FSEvents.

### How copying works, and why animated stickers stay animated

F4 puts the file itself on the clipboard: its file URL (`public.file-url`) and its raw bytes under the file's type (`com.compuserve.gif`, `public.png`, `public.jpeg`, `org.webmproject.webp`). It never puts a decoded image there, which would flatten a GIF to one frame. So Slack, Discord, Telegram, WhatsApp Desktop, Messages, Mail and most chat apps paste the animated GIF. An app that accepts only plain images may paste the first frame; that is the app's limit.

### Menu bar menu

F4 has no Settings window: like Maramao's, its menu bar menu holds the options. In order:

Open F4 (with a line under it only if macOS refused the F4 key because another app owns it) · Recent Stickers (the last 5 copied, with a thumbnail; a click copies one again without opening the panel) · Folders ▸ (New Folder…, then each folder of the library ▸ Rename…, Move to Trash, with a confirmation that counts its stickers) · Packs ▸ (shown when F4 lists a pack: each pack is a switch: turning it on downloads the pack's stickers from their links (a getstickerpack.com pack link brings all its stickers) into a folder of the library named after the pack, never overwriting a file; turning it off moves that folder to the Trash after a confirmation) · Options (below, rarely shown) · How to Add Stickers… (the window shown on the first launch: copy, fn F4, ⌘V; also the ⓘ button in the panel) · Check for Updates… (or "Update to Version x…" once Sparkle found one) · Quit F4 (Command-Q). The icon is always shown; opening F4 again from Finder or Spotlight shows the panel, and `f4://settings` opens this menu under the pointer.

### Options

| Option | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Show Starter Pack | The stickers built into F4, after the user's own; shown only with a folder other than F4's own library, which holds a copy of them | On |

That is the only option. The shortcut is always F4 (fn F4 on a Mac keyboard) and cannot be changed; F4 always starts at login. F4 needs no permission: the global shortcut uses Carbon `RegisterEventHotKey`, which needs no Accessibility, Input Monitoring or Screen Recording, and F4 never pastes for the user.

Preferences are stored in the `com.kkratterf.f4` defaults domain (`~/Library/Preferences/com.kkratterf.f4.plist`): `memeFolderPath`, `seededStarterFolders` (the starter folders already copied into F4's library, each once; up to 0.4 `didSeedLibrary` meant Emoji and F4), `didRegisterLoginItem` (F4 added itself to the login items once), `didRemoveRetiredStarter` (the Emoji and F4 starter folders of 0.6 were moved out, once), `didShowWelcome` (the "Add your stickers" window was shown on the first launch), `showStarterPack`, `downloadedPacks` (the packs switched on), `panelPosition` (where the panel was dragged, as fractions of the screen), `favouriteMemes`, `recentMemes` (file paths). Change them from the menu rather than with `defaults write` while F4 is running.

### Easter eggs

The empty state draws the basito face in code. A file named `.basito.png`, `.basito.gif` or `.basito.jpg` in the sticker folder replaces it with the user's own. Typing some lines from Boris, The Office and old internet memes in the search field, or the Konami code (up up down down left right left right B A) in the panel, shows a banner and sometimes does something to the grid. The list is in the source (`Sources/F4Core/EasterEggs.swift`); part of the fun is finding them, so do not recite them all unless asked.

### Raycast

The F4 Raycast extension, in https://github.com/kkratterf/f4/tree/main/raycast, has one command, "Search Stickers", that searches the same folder as the app (F4's library, or a folder set in the extension preferences) and copies or pastes a sticker as a file, so animated stickers stay animated there too. It is not in the Raycast Store yet; install it from the repository with `cd raycast && npm install && npm run dev`.

## Automation: f4:// URLs

Anything that can open a URL can drive F4: Shortcuts ("Open URLs"), Raycast or Alfred quicklinks, a Stream Deck, AppleScript, a shell script or an AI agent with a terminal (`open "f4://copy?name=this%20is%20fine"`). Query values are URL-encoded; `+` also counts as a space.

| URL | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `f4://open` | Shows the panel |
| `f4://search?q=this%20is%20fine` | Shows the panel with the search typed in |
| `f4://copy?name=this%20is%20fine` | Copies the best match without showing the panel (beeps if nothing matches) |
| `f4://reload` | Rescans the sticker folder |
| `f4://settings` | Opens the menu bar menu under the pointer, where the options are |

- `f4://copy` copies the sticker the panel would show first for that search: the best fuzzy match, with favourites and then recently copied stickers winning a tie. It counts as a copy (it moves to the top of the recents) and shows the same toast. Nothing matches: F4 beeps and the clipboard is left alone.
- Commands are case-insensitive. `f4:open` and a trailing slash work too; `q` and `query` are accepted for search, `name`, `q` and `query` for copy.
- If F4 is not running, the URL starts it and then does what it asks (a copy waits for the first folder scan, and shows nothing).
- Unknown commands are ignored.

## Update

F4 updates itself with Sparkle: it checks https://f4.kkratter.com/appcast.xml about once a day, offers the new version, and installs it in one click after the user confirms. Updates are signed (EdDSA) and verified before install. "Check for Updates…" in the menu bar menu checks right away. With automatic checks off (Sparkle asks on the second launch), install a new version by hand: drag the new DMG's app over the old one, or run the install one-liner again. Settings, favourites and memes are kept.

Pre-release versions (for example `0.3.0-beta.1`) are published on GitHub only; automatic updates and Homebrew offer stable versions.

## Uninstall

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kkratterf/f4/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall
```

It quits F4, deletes `F4.app` and its settings (`defaults delete com.kkratterf.f4`). With Homebrew: `brew uninstall --cask f4`, or `brew uninstall --zap --cask f4` to remove the settings and caches too. By hand: quit F4 from the menu bar, delete `F4.app`, optionally `defaults delete com.kkratterf.f4`. The meme folder is never touched.

## Troubleshooting

- "Nothing happens when I press F4", or F4 opens Spotlight or Launchpad: on a Mac keyboard the top row sends media keys unless fn is held. Press fn-F4, or turn on "Use F1, F2, etc. keys as standard function keys" in System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > Function Keys. Also check F4 is running (the F4 key icon in the menu bar); another app may already own the F4 key (the menu then says so under Open F4).
- Upgrading from an older version: a shortcut picked there is ignored since 0.4.3; the shortcut is F4.
- "The panel says No stickers yet": the folder is empty, missing, or holds only unsupported files. Paste or drop stickers in the panel, or switch on a pack in the menu bar's Packs.
- "The GIF pastes as a still image": the receiving app takes only images. Most chat apps paste the animation; try pasting into a message field rather than an image editor.
- "macOS says F4 is damaged or cannot be verified": see First launch and Gatekeeper above.
- "No Check for Updates item": F4 is running as a bare binary (`swift run`) rather than as `F4.app`. Install a release, or build the app bundle.
- Bugs and ideas: https://github.com/kkratterf/f4/issues/new/choose. Security issues: https://github.com/kkratterf/f4/blob/main/SECURITY.md

## Build from source

Needs macOS 14+ and Xcode 15+ (Swift 5.9).

```sh
git clone https://github.com/kkratterf/f4
cd f4
swift build
swift test
scripts/build-app.sh release   # dist/F4.app
open dist/F4.app
```

`scripts/build-dmg.sh` builds the DMG. `swift run F4` starts the bare binary without the updater; `dist/F4.app` checks for updates like a release and replaces itself with the next official version.

## What F4 does not do (yet)

- No HEIC, PNG sequences or video files; those are planned. Animated WebP stickers show their first frame in the grid and still paste animated.
- No cloud sync and no search on the internet. Packs are downloaded from links, never bundled: F4 shows only files in the user's library.
- No direct import of the stickers saved inside WhatsApp yet: add a `.wastickers` pack file, or copy a sticker in WhatsApp (right-click → Copy) and press Command-V in the panel.
- One sticker folder at a time (with subfolders).
- No tags beyond folder names, no OCR of the text inside images.
- No Shortcuts actions, command line tool or MCP server yet; they are planned. Until then scripts and AI agents use the `f4://` URLs above, the sticker folder directly (it is a plain folder of files) or the Raycast extension.

The roadmap is the issue list, labelled by version: https://github.com/kkratterf/f4/issues
